items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) Explain why a chloride ion, Cl⁻, is larger than a chlorine atom. (b) Explain why atomic radius decreases across Period 3.
items.answer: (a) Cl⁻ has an extra electron in the same outer shell; increased repulsion between electrons and the same nuclear charge (17 protons for 18 electrons) means the electron cloud expands. (b) Nuclear charge (number of protons) increases while shielding stays roughly the same (same number of inner shells), so the outer electrons are pulled closer to the nucleus.
items.markingKey: (a) extra electron, more repulsion; same nuclear charge [2] (b) increasing nuclear charge; similar shielding / same shell [2]

items.stem: The boiling points of propan-1-ol, CH₃CH₂CH₂OH, and propanone, CH₃COCH₃, are 97 °C and 56 °C. Explain the difference in terms of intermolecular forces.
items.answer: Propan-1-ol has the higher boiling point: propan-1-ol molecules form hydrogen bonds (H bonded to N, O or F with a lone pair on a neighbour), which are much stronger than the permanent dipole–permanent dipole forces between propanone molecules.
items.markingKey: identifies forces in each substance [1]; compares strength with reason (electrons / H bonding / polarity / shape) [1]
